summary: Extends the PCEP association mechanism so that sets of Label Switched Paths can be linked to a higher-level Virtual Network requested by a customer or application. This helps manage a virtual network using the PCE architecture.

plainLanguage.summary: Many separate roads are tagged as belonging to one customer's private road system, so they can be managed as a group.

questions: how to group lsps into a virtual network
what is a vn association group
subtitle: Tag a set of PCEP-controlled paths as belonging to one customer's Virtual Network so a PCE can manage them together.

tldr.problem: A customer or application can ask for a Virtual Network (VN) built from many Label Switched Paths (LSPs), but PCEP had no way to say which LSPs belong to which VN.
tldr.mechanism: It defines a new association type, the VN Association Group (VNAG, type 7), plus a mandatory VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV (type 65) that carries a human-readable VN identifier.
tldr.outcome: A PCE can now optimize, reoptimize and apply policy to all LSPs of a VN together. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 9358 is a Proposed Standard (February 2023) and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the association mechanism of RFC 8697.

sections.title: Why LSPs Need a Virtual Network Tag
sections.content:
The Path Computation Element Communication Protocol (PCEP) lets Path Computation Elements (PCEs) compute paths for Path Computation Clients (PCCs). Stateful PCE extensions let the PCE also know about active paths and their reserved resources, and RFC 8697 adds a generic way to group LSPs into associations.

A Virtual Network (VN) is a customer view of the traffic-engineering network, as described in the ACTN framework. In that architecture the child PCE is identified with the Provisioning Network Controller (PNC) and the parent PCE with the Multi-Domain Service Coordinator (MDSC).

The gap is that a PCE cannot tell which LSPs make up a given VN. With that knowledge it could optimize all LSPs of the VN at once, and take VN-specific actions such as relaxing constraints, applying policy or setting default behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: A customer has many little roads that make up their private network. Until now the road planners had no label saying which roads go together.

sections.title: The VN Association Group
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new association group, the VN Association Group (VNAG). It reuses the ASSOCIATION object from RFC 8697 with a new Association Type value of 7, "VN Association". An ASSOCIATION object with that type is called a VNAG object, and its Association Identifier is the VNAG Identifier.

Grouping helps in two ways the RFC names. For path computation, the PCE can judge the impact of one LSP on the others in the same VN and apply an optimization criterion across all of them. For path reoptimization, the PCE can use algorithms that consider every LSP of the VN and optimize them together.

Local policy on the PCE defines the computation and optimization behavior for the VN. An LSP MUST NOT belong to more than one VNAG. If a PCEP message holds more than one VNAG object, the receiver MUST process the first and ignore the others.
sections.plainLanguage: All the roads of one customer get the same sticker number. Each road can only wear one such sticker, and if a road shows up with two, the planner only reads the first.

sections.title: How the Parent and Child PCEs Use It
sections.content:
The association is meant for a PCEP session between a parent PCE (MDSC) and a child PCE (PNC). The parent receives a VN creation request from its customer. The VN is identified by the association parameters or by the Virtual Network Identifier in the VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV, and may span one domain or several.

The parent sends a PCInitiate message carrying the VNAG object, which binds the LSP being instantiated at the child PCE to the VN. The VN association information MUST be included in the first PCRpt message. When the instantiated LSP changes, the child PCE reports it with a PCRpt whose VNAG object shows the LSP-to-VN relationship. When a VN changes at the parent because of a customer request, the parent sends a PCUpd message to each affected child.

In a multi-domain case, different child PCEs control different domains, and border nodes stitch the segments together to set up a cross-domain tunnel.
sections.plainLanguage: The big boss planner tells each regional planner, 'build this road and mark it as part of customer X's network'. The regional planners report back using the same mark whenever something changes.

sections.title: Advertising Support and Identifier Rules
sections.content:
A PCEP speaker MUST include the VN Association Type (7) in the ASSOC-Type-List TLV of its OPEN object before it uses a VNAG object. A speaker that does not support the type returns a PCErr with Error-Type 26 (Association Error) and Error-value 1 (Association Type is not supported), as RFC 8697 specifies.

VNAG IDs are dynamic. They are created by the parent PCE (MDSC) based on VN operations. Operator configuration of VNAG IDs is not supported, so type 7 MUST NOT appear in the Operator-configured Association Range TLV. If an implementation does see it there, it MUST ignore the associated Start-Assoc-ID and Range values.
sections.plainLanguage: Before using the sticker, each side says 'I know how to read these stickers'. The numbers on the stickers are handed out by the boss planner, never typed in by hand.

sections.title: The VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV
sections.content:
The VNAG uses the generic ASSOCIATION object. The RFC adds one new mandatory TLV, the VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV, which carries the Virtual Network Identifier. The existing VENDOR-INFORMATION-TLV from RFC 7470 may optionally be used alongside it for vendor-specific behavior.

The TLV has Type 65 (16 bits), a 16-bit Length that MUST be greater than 0, and a variable-length Virtual Network Identifier. The TLV MUST be zero-padded to a 4-octet boundary.

The identifier is a symbolic name that uniquely identifies the VN. It SHOULD be a string of printable ASCII characters (0x20 to 0x7E) without a NULL terminator. It MAY be specified by the customer, set by operator policy, or auto-generated by the PCEP speaker. Implementations use it to map the VNAG to its LSPs.
sections.plainLanguage: The tag is a name written in plain letters, like 'Customer X's roads', padded out so it fits neatly in its box.

sections.title: Errors When the TLV Is Missing or Wrong
sections.content:
If a PCEP speaker receives a VNAG object without the VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV, it MUST send a PCErr with Error-Type 6 (Mandatory Object missing) and Error-value 18 (VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV missing), and close the session.

If a VNAG object has a TLV that violates the rules in the RFC, the speaker MUST send a PCErr with Error-Type 10 (Reception of an invalid object) and Error-value 11 (Malformed object), and MUST close the PCEP session.
sections.plainLanguage: A sticker with no name on it is rejected, and so is a badly written one. In both cases the planners stop talking and tell each other why.

sections.title: Security and Manageability
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 5440, RFC 8231 and RFC 8281 apply, as do those of RFC 8697 about a malicious PCEP speaker. Securing the PCEP session with TLS is RECOMMENDED.

On the management side, an operator MUST be allowed to mark LSPs that belong to the same VN, which could also be automatic from VN configuration. The PCEP YANG module should support associations including the VN association. The RFC says it adds no new liveness-detection or verification requirements beyond RFC 5440.
sections.plainLanguage: Since a fake planner could lie about the stickers, the planners are advised to talk over a locked, private line.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA assigned three values for this RFC. In the ASSOCIATION Type Field subregistry, value 7 is "VN Association". In the PCEP TLV Type Indicators subregistry, value 65 is VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV. In the PCEP-ERROR Object Error Types and Values subregistry, Error-Type 6 (Mandatory Object missing) gets Error-value 18, "VIRTUAL-NETWORK-TLV missing".
sections.plainLanguage: The official number keeper wrote down the new sticker type, the new name tag type and the new error message in the master list.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the value in octets; MUST be greater than 0.

fields.name: Virtual Network Identifier
fields.desc: Variable-length symbolic VN name, zero-padded to a 4-octet boundary.
